what_its_for: Cefprozil is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections such as ear infections, throat infections (like strep throat), sinus infections, and certain skin infections. It works by killing the bacteria causing your infection. It does NOT work for viral infections like the cold or flu.
how_to_take: Take cefprozil by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or snack. If you are using the liquid (suspension), shake the bottle well before each use and measure your dose carefully with the measuring spoon or oral syringe that came with the medication — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water.
dosing: Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed for as many days as directed, even if you start feeling better before you finish. Stopping early can allow the infection to come back and may make it harder to treat. Typical treatment courses last 10 days, but your doctor will tell you the right length for your specific infection.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tablets at room temperature, away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep them in a tightly closed container. For the liquid suspension: store it in the refrigerator. Do NOT freeze it. Throw away any unused liquid after 14 days. Keep all medications out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid skipping doses or stopping the medication early, even if you feel better. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all other medications you take, especially blood thinners like warfarin, since cefprozil may affect how they work. Avoid taking antacids or other medications within a few hours unless your doctor approves. Let your doctor know if you drink alcohol, as it can increase the risk of stomach upset.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you experience: a serious allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, trouble breathing or swallowing, dizziness); severe or watery diarrhea that does not go away or contains blood — this could be a serious bowel infection; yellowing of the skin or eyes; dark urine; unusual bruising or bleeding; seizures; or if your symptoms do not improve after a few days of treatment or they get worse.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting cefprozil. However, it is very important to take the full course of treatment even if you feel completely well. If you do not notice any improvement after 3 days, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease, your doctor may give you a lower dose or have you take the medication less often. Always tell your doctor about any kidney problems. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medication. Children: Cefprozil is approved for use in children. The liquid form is often used for young children. The dose is based on the child's weight. Older adults: Older adults with kidney problems may need a dose adjustment. Penicillin allergy: Tell your doctor if you have ever had an allergic reaction to penicillin or any other antibiotic, as there is a small chance of cross-reaction with cefprozil.
